context.synopsis: On November 7, 2018, Trump fired Attorney General Jeff Sessions the day after the midterm elections, ending a months-long public humiliation campaign in which Trump had repeatedly attacked Sessions publicly for recusing himself from the Russia investigation. It would "prioritize" federal prosecution of state election officials who send or receive ballots to non-citizens or others ineligible to vote. The order gives DHS and USPS new roles in screening state voter rolls — creating federal control over what has historically been a state-administered process.
context.rationale: Using the Postal Service and DHS to screen voter rolls and threatening prosecution of state election officials represents federal takeover of elections.
